text:
mina: quick note: found a redaction inconsistency in java sample-app when toggling log level at runtime — structured JSON logs redact reqId but console text formatter still prints it on retry lines.

mina: repro steps:
1) start sample-app with LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG and otel log hook enabled
2) change level to WARN via admin endpoint (runtime)
3) trigger failing downstream call -> retry handler logs retry
4) observe console message includes reqId while JSON encoder has reqId=nullified

diego: that suggests the RedactionFilter is attached only to the JSON encoder/appender and gets lost when appenders are reconfigured on level change. which logback version + our redaction wrapper?

mina: logback 1.4.6, redaction-encoder v1.2.0. console appender is reconstructed by our admin endpoint logic when changing level. the new instance wasn't wired with the filter.

tara: exact logs:
WARN  DownstreamClient - request failed reqId=req-7f4b
INFO  RetryHandler - retry attempt=2 message=retrying reqId=req-7f4b
{"ts":"...","level":"WARN","reqId":null,"user":"u9"}

mina: so structured redaction works but plain text leaks. quick mitigation: reuse the same appender instances on level change OR ensure admin endpoint reapplies filters after rebind. i'll open a small PR in sampleapps/java-telemetry with failing test.

ci-bot: queued job: samples/java-telemetry (#PR-4601) - matrix jdk11/jdk17 - console+json encoders. ETA ~10m

qa-bot: note added to INC-4981: java console redaction gap. tests to include runtime toggle scenario + retry flow.

diego: long-term we should implement a TurboFilter in logback that runs before formatting so we don't have to wire filters per-appender. careful about perf: do a cheap prefix check for "req" then run regex only on matches.

tara: agreed. parity note: python and go SDKs already use pre-formatter hooks so they don't miss console lines. marking as sdk-parity and telemetry-refactor.

mina: assigning P2 for now; if ops finds runtime toggles enabled in prod java clusters escalate to P1. :eyes:
